channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Governo Lula decide reduzir tributos sobre gasolina para combater efeitos da guerra no Iră
item.description: The Lula government announced a reduction in PIS/Cofins taxes on gasoline to counteract the impact of the Iran war on fuel prices. The measure is part of a broader package to control inflation, though specific details of the tax cut have not yet been disclosed.

item.title: Crusoé: Lula convoca delegados da PF que estão “fingindo trabalhar”
item.description: President Lula (PT) stated that he ordered Justice and Public Security Minister Wellington César Lima to summon all Federal Police delegates who are "pretending to work," citing alleged absences or low productivity. He said he had previously requested the minister issue a note calling these servants back to duty.

item.title: Zema diz que Brasil deveria ter lei para banir o 13º andar
item.description: Romeu Zema, a pré-candidate for president from the Novo party, suggested Brazil should pass a law to ban the 13th floor in buildings, claiming the number 13 is associated with the Workers' Party (PT) and considered bad luck. In a video posted on X, he advocated skipping from the 12th to the 14th floor, as done in some countries, and asked social media users what they thought.

item.title: Governo barra Terrabras e abre racha com PT no Congresso
item.description: The Lula government decided to block the creation of the state-owned Terrabras in the critical minerals framework, causing a rift with PT congressmen who advocate for greater state participation in the mineral sector. The decision, made in a meeting at the Palácio da Alvorada, prioritizes establishing a critical minerals council linked to the presidency as an alternative to a public company. Congressional allies admit the proposals are unlikely to advance in 2026, with possible revival only in a potential fourth term of Lula.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula entrega prêmio de incentivo à leitura
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) attends the World Book Day ceremony in Brasília, where he presents the 9th Vivaleitura Award and signs, alongside the Ministers of Education and Culture, the ordinance establishing the National Book and Reading Plan 2026-2035. The event aims to highlight outstanding reading promotion projects and set guidelines for public policy in the area over the next decade.

item.title: Lei Antifacção não vai barrar votos de presos provisórios em 2026, decide TSE
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) ruled that the Anti-Facão Law, which bans voting by provisional and temporary prisoners, does not apply to the 2026 elections due to the principle of electoral annuality. The court stated that legislative changes cannot be implemented this year due to technical time constraints and lack of integration between electoral and security systems, so prisoner voter registration and voting in prisons will remain in place for this year's election.

item.title: Lula usa novo atrito com EUA para retomar discurso de soberania, faz gesto à PF e endossa retórica de 'guerra contra o crime'
item.description: Lula used the diplomatic friction with the U.S. over the withdrawal of an FBI agent at Trump’s request to revive his national sovereignty narrative and announce the hiring of 1,000 approved candidates for the Federal Police, framing it as part of a 'war on organized crime'. He praised PF Director-General Andrei Rodrigues and stressed the need for more federal police to arrest criminals, amid the presidential race against Flavio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Governo Lula torrou ao menos R$ 860 milhões com a COP30
item.description: The Lula government's Civil House reported that direct spending on organizing COP30 amounted to at least 860 million Brazilian reais, including contracts, agreements, and projects managed by the event's Extraordinary Secretariat. The figure was disclosed in response to a Chamber of Deputies request and covers 16 detailed expense categories.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes ironiza sotaque de Zema ao comentar inquérito das fake news
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes mocked the accent of former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema, saying he speaks a 'dialect close to Portuguese' and compared his speech to Tetum, the language of Timor-Leste, during remarks on Zema's inclusion in the fake news inquiry over puppet shows and deepfake videos satirizing justices. Zema responded by expressing pride in his roots, accusing the Court of corruption, and stating the ridicule offends millions of Mineiros, reinforcing his campaign narrative against the 'untouchables' of the judiciary.

item.title: Lula: qualidade do agro é essencial para ampliar exportações
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva emphasized the need to improve the quality and sophistication of Brazilian agricultural products to expand exports and compete in more demanding international markets. He stated that large-scale production and diversity are insufficient without technological and quality excellence, highlighting Embrapa's role in driving innovation. Lula also noted that every R$1 invested in Embrapa yields R$27 in social return, with the agency contributing R$125 billion to Brazil's 2025 agricultural GDP.

item.title: Nunes diz que críticos da “Times Square” de SP não precisam visitá-la
item.description: São Paulo Mayor Ricardo Nunes defended the Boulevard São João project, inspired by Times Square, stating critics do not need to visit the site. The project includes installing four LED panels with 2,000 m² of screens, restoring the Ipiranga and São João avenues area, and will be funded by advertising, with 70% of content dedicated to digital arts and cultural events. Approved by the Urban Landscape Protection Commission, the initiative has the support of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas.

item.title: Bancada do PT reafirma defesa por estatal de terras raras
item.description: The PT caucus in the Chamber reaffirmed its support for creating a state-owned company, called Terrabras, to explore critical minerals and rare earths in the country. This stance comes one day after President Lula closed the issue against the proposal, indicating internal divergence within the government. The initiative aims to ensure technological sovereignty and reduce dependence on strategic imports.

item.title: TSE decide que preso provisório pode votar neste ano, mesmo com a Lei Antifacção
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) ruled that pretrial detainees may vote in the 2026 elections, maintaining voter registration and polling stations in prisons. The unanimous decision was grounded in the principle of electoral annuality, which bars the application of electoral law changes within one year of an election, rendering the Anti-Facção Law inapplicable for this cycle. The TSE also cited the May 6 voter registration deadline and lack of automated integration between electoral and security systems as technical barriers to immediate enforcement.

item.title: Governo reajusta preços de referência do vale-gás em 22 estados; veja os aumentos
item.description: The Lula government adjusted the voucher value of the Gás do Povo program in 22 states, with increases of up to R$10, to counter the effects of the Iran war on energy input prices. The benefit, provided to Bolsa Família families and those with per capita income up to half a minimum wage, saw its budget expanded by R$300 million. Acre, DF, ES, RJ, and MT did not receive an adjustment.

item.title: Ação penal contra Eduardo Bolsonaro no STF entra na reta final
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes has opened the period for final arguments in the criminal case against former federal deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro, accused of obstruction of justice. The Prosecutor General's Office has 15 days to submit its position, which may call for acquittal or conviction, followed by Eduardo's defense. The case could be ready for judgment by the end of May, stemming from Eduardo's advocacy for U.S. tariffs and sanctions against Brazil in retaliation for legal proceedings against his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Deputados do PSOL acionam a PGR contra venda de mineradora de terras raras em Goiás e pedem investigação sobre Caiado
item.description: PSOL deputies filed a representation with the PGR against former Goiás governor and presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado, challenging the legality of the sale of Serra Verde mineradora to USA Rare Earth for US$2.8 billion. They demand the annulment of the deal and an investigation into alleged constitutional overreach by Caiado, while also requesting information from the Ministries of Mines and Energy and Foreign Relations on whether federal authorization was granted.

item.title: Alerj aciona STF para que Douglas Ruas assuma governo interino do Rio de forma ‘imediata’
item.description: The Rio de Janeiro State Legislative Assembly (Alerj) has asked the Supreme Federal Court (STF) to immediately install state deputy Douglas Ruas (PL), elected president of the House, as interim governor, arguing his election constitutes a 'new fact' altering the interim governance situation. Currently, interim power is held by Judge Ricardo Couto of the TJ-RJ, who has dismissed over 600 commissioned staff. The opposition, led by the PDT, challenges Ruas’s election as illegitimate, citing procedural irregularities and rushed voting rules.

item.title: Youtuber alvo de Moraes no 8 de janeiro quer ser deputado federal
item.description: Bismark Fugazza, a businessman and influencer under investigation by the Brazilian Supreme Court for alleged involvement in the January 8 attacks, announced his pre-candidacy for federal deputy from Santa Catarina under the Podemos party, despite being subject to precautionary measures that restrict his movement and communication.

item.title: Ciclo pós-garantia de inversores solares exige manutenção
item.description: Brazil's solar energy market is entering a post-warranty phase, with thousands of inverters installed between 2018 and 2022 now facing technical failures after their five-year factory warranties expire. Demand for specialized maintenance is growing exponentially to prevent costly downtime, especially amid rising tariffs and new net-metering rules. Companies like Ozora Soluções emphasize 'Strategic After-Sales' service, using advanced diagnostics and component-level repairs to ensure continuous operation of solar plants.

item.title: A aposta que Raquel Lyra faz para fisgar votos de Lula em Pernambuco e virar o jogo contra João Campos
item.description: Governor Raquel Lyra (PSD) is attempting to close the gap in polls against former Recife mayor João Campos (PSB) in Pernambuco, betting on winning over part of Lula’s electorate through her administration’s deliverables and the support of 142 of the state’s 184 mayors. She aims to capture around 35% of Lula’s votes in the state to overturn her deficit and retain office. To achieve this, Lyra has adjusted her rhetoric, now praising the federal government in pursuit of a strategic alliance with the PT.

item.title: O novo prazo para a PF concluir inquérito contra Monark
item.description: Supreme Federal Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes granted the Federal Police an additional 60 days to conclude the inquiry against influencer Monark, citing technical limitations in data analysis. The case involves alleged non-compliance with judicial orders related to profiles accused of instigating the January 8, 2023, coup attempts. The PF states the work is in an advanced stage following file extraction.

item.title: Pré-candidatos de direita e estudantes entram em confronto na UFMG
item.description: State deputy candidates Douglas Garcia (União Brasil-SP) and Marília Amaral (PL-MG) were involved in a physical confrontation with students at UFMG during a political activity displaying a sign that read 'Is Lula better than Bolsonaro for Brazil? Pix of R$500 to whoever proves it'. The incident took place at the Fafich campus in Pampulha, escalating into physical altercations, with video showing Garcia exchanging punches with a protester. UFMG stated the political content recording was not officially notified and reaffirmed its commitment to a plural, safe, and institutionally organized environment.

item.title: TSE decide que proibição de voto a presos provisórios não vale para eleição de 2026
item.description: The TSE unanimously ruled that the voting ban for pretrial detainees under the Anti-Corruption Law does not apply to the 2026 elections, allowing this group to vote in the upcoming poll. The decision was made on April 23, 2026, at 14:12, and directly impacts the expansion of the electorate for the next elections.

item.title: Lula quer volta ao trabalho de agentes da PF afastados
item.description: President Lula ordered Federal Police agents who are away from duty to return to work, except for state secretaries, insisting all must act against organized crime. The directive follows a decree creating 1,000 new PF positions to fully staff the force for the first time, after a diplomatic rift with the U.S. over the expulsion of delegate Marcelo Ivo de Carvalho, tied to the Alexandre Ramagem case. Lula also criticized Donald Trump, framing U.S. warmongering as opposed to Brazil’s goal of teaching Africa peace through food production.

item.title: Lula diz estar otimista e critica UE por travar acordo com Mercosul
item.description: President Lula said he is optimistic about the Mercosul-European Union agreement, criticizing the EU's legal challenge as 'jealous people' who fail to recognize Brazil's productive capacity. He noted the agreement's provisional implementation begins May 1st and stressed the need to improve product quality to compete in Europe, while defending Embrapa and countering social media misinformation.

item.title: Moraes abre prazo para alegações finais de Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes has opened the deadline for final arguments in the criminal case against Eduardo Bolsonaro, accused of attempting to interfere with the trial of the coup attempt by pressuring U.S. authorities to sanction Brazilian officials. The former congressman, residing in the U.S. and having presented no defense witnesses, had the indictment accepted by the STF’s 1st Chamber in November 2025. The case now proceeds to final statements from the prosecution and defense before the final judgment.

item.title: Moraes abre prazo para apresentação de alegações finais em processo contra Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes has granted Eduardo Bolsonaro a 15-day deadline to submit final arguments in a criminal case alleging procedural coercion. The Prosecutor General’s Office (PGR) and the Federal Public Defender’s Office (DPU) will each have the same period to respond. The case examines Eduardo’s alleged coordination with the U.S. government to secure amnesty for his father, Jair Bolsonaro, including proposals such as a 50% tariff on Brazilian exports to the U.S. and invoking the Magnitsky Act against STF justices.

item.title: Lula fala em deixar “mentirosos nus” e mira Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) accused opponents of spreading misinformation and stated that, with the start of the electoral campaign, he will 'expose the liars' and 'leave them naked before the cameras', directing criticism at Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ). He emphasized that he is not yet in an election period but praised Embrapa's credibility and urged supporters to counter misinformation on social media. The PL filed a representation with the TSE against Lula for alleged premature electioneering, while the PT intensifies its communication strategy with national TV ads and a party congress.

item.title: Lula indica que ampliará ataques na eleição e promete deixar 'mentirosos nus' diante das câmeras
item.description: President Lula (PT) criticized Donald Trump in a speech and signaled he will intensify attacks against political adversaries in the 2026 election campaign, promising to expose 'liars naked' before the cameras. The remarks were made on Thursday (23) and suggest a more aggressive political communication strategy.

item.title: Damares cobra atuação de Lula em investigações sobre venda ilegal de remédios oncológicos
item.description: Senator Damares Alves (Republicans) called on the Lula government to respond to a scheme involving the illegal diversion and sale of high-cost medicines, revealed in Operation Alto Custo by the DF Civil Police. She sent an official letter to Health Minister Alexandre Padilha to confirm whether criminally sourced drugs entered the SUS and filed an information request in the Senate. The investigation found a criminal network that stole, tampered with, and resold cancer, autoimmune, and transplant medications, moving R$22 million in fake invoices and seizing medicines worth R$4 million.

item.title: Desaprovação de Lula chega a 50% no Lulômetro
item.description: President Lula's (PT) disapproval rating reached 50% for the first time in the Lulômetro, a daily tracking poll conducted by O Antagonista and Real Time Big Data. The government is rated as 'bad/terrible' by 50%, 'excellent/good' by 27%, and 'fair' by 22%, with only 1% responding 'don't know/no answer'. This marks the worst evaluation recorded for the petista since the tracking began.

item.title: “O grupo de Bolsonaro sai fortalecido”, diz cientista político sobre nova crise internacional de Lula
item.description: The Brazilian government adopted the principle of reciprocity in response to the withdrawal of credentials of an American agent following the return of a Brazilian delegate involved in the Ramagem case, a measure deemed inevitable and correct by political scientist Leonardo Paz. He assessed that the episode temporarily strengthened Bolsonaro's group, showing it still holds some influence in the White House, but that this impact is likely limited without further developments.

item.title: Lula propõe levar jabuticaba para Trump: "Vou tentar levar uma para acalmá-lo"
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said he intends to gift Donald Trump a jabuticaba tree during a future trip, suggesting the fruit could have calming effects to help soothe the former U.S. president. The comment was made at the Embrapa-organized 'Brasil na Mesa' fair in Planaltina, following Lula’s return from an official trip to Europe. Lula also emphasized Brazil’s biodiversity potential and criticized the nation’s tendency to prioritize exports over its large domestic market.

item.title: Zema x Gilmar: cientista político aponta quem sai ganhando e perdendo com o embate
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema is using criticism of the Supreme Court as part of an electoral strategy to attract conservative and far-right voters, according to political scientist Leonardo Paz. Minister Gilmar Mendes’ judicial response may unintentionally amplify Zema’s visibility, creating ambiguous political effects. Paz warns that such institutional confrontations erode public trust and create opportunities for opportunistic politicians to exploit democratic fatigue.

item.title: Restrições da Lei Raul Jungmann não vigoram para as Eleições 2026
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) ruled that amendments introduced by the Raul Jungmann Law (Law No. 15.358/2026) to the Electoral Code cannot be applied to the 2026 elections, as they violate the principle of electoral annuality. The unanimous decision preserves voter registration and polling station setup in prison facilities, ensuring the changes will only take effect in future elections.

item.title: Empresas criticam e governistas elogiam avanço do fim da 6 X 1
item.description: The approval of the admissibility of the PEC proposing the end of the 6x1 work schedule (reducing the weekly workload to 40 hours) sparked criticism from business associations, warning of inflation risks, job losses, and reduced competitiveness, particularly in industrial sectors. Government supporters praised the move as fulfillment of a campaign promise by President Lula. The proposal now awaits the installation of a special committee by the Chamber's presidency to proceed.

item.title: Alerj pede que STF transfira governo interino do RJ para Douglas Ruas
item.description: The Rio de Janeiro State Legislative Assembly (Alerj) asked the STF to transfer the state's interim government from Judge Ricardo Couto to the new Legislative President, Deputy Douglas Ruas (PL-RJ), arguing that his election on April 17 and inauguration on April 22 reopens the succession issue. The request is made in ADI 7942 (Justice Luiz Fux as rapporteur), while the injunction keeping Couto in office comes from Rcl 92644 (Justice Cristiano Zanin as rapporteur), whose joint judgment was suspended by a request for view from Justice Flávio Dino on April 9. Alerj claims the new legislative presidency constitutes a supervenient fact justifying a new deliberation, expressly reserved by the Court.

item.title: Gilmar defende inquérito das fake news até pelo menos as eleições
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes advocated for keeping the fake news investigation open at least until the 2026 elections, stating it remains necessary and that the Court is being vilipended. He referenced attacks by the rapporteur of the Organized Crime CPI and forwarded a crime report to the PGR against presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema for allegedly dishonoring the Court in a social media series. The inquiry, launched in 2019, investigates criminal offenses against the Court and its members, with no set end date.

item.title: Moraes estende em 60 dias investigação sobre Monark por desobediência a ordem judicial
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes extended by 60 days the investigation into influencer Monark for repeatedly violating court orders to block his social media accounts and refrain from spreading false claims about electoral integrity. The Federal Police requested the extension, stating that Monark continued using platforms like Rumble, Spotify, and others to monetize antidemocratic content despite judicial blocks. The case is connected to the broader investigation into the January 8, 2023, attacks on Brazil’s government buildings.

item.title: TSE autoriza descentralização de recursos para Eleições 2026 no exterior
item.description: The TSE approved the decentralization of R$13.285.832,70 for the 2026 elections abroad, allowing the rental of properties outside Brazilian consular offices to set up 65 voting sections. The measure, requested by the MRE and TRE-DF, ensures voting rights for Brazilians overseas and complies with the Electoral Code’s minimum requirement of 30 registered voters per section.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia rejeita habeas corpus para manter Bolsonaro em prisão domiciliar
item.description: Supreme Federal Tribunal Minister Cármen Lúcia rejected a habeas corpus petition seeking to extend Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest beyond the initial 90-day period granted by Alexandre de Moraes. The ruling was based on the lack of authorization from Bolsonaro's official legal defense and the principle that habeas corpus does not apply against acts of a STF minister. Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year and three-month sentence for leading an attempted coup, currently under house arrest for health reasons.

item.title: Brasil na Hannover Messe: entre o ufanismo e a entrega econômica
item.description: Brazil's participation in Hannover Messe 2026 featured announcements of approximately €2 billion in low-carbon hydrogen and derivative investments in Rio Grande do Norte, with President Lula da Silva and ApexBrasil leading the agenda to position the country in global green value chains. Despite the financial scale and symbolic weight, sector experts note that project realization hinges on regulatory frameworks, long-term financing, and stable demand, with many viewing the event as a platform for signaling intent rather than immediate contracts. ApexBrasil expresses optimism contingent on maturation timelines and highlights the Mercosul-EU agreement as a near-term catalyst, while cautioning against European tendencies to judge Brazil’s tropical agricultural model by their own standards.

item.title: Lula diz ter chamado delegados que estão 'fingindo trabalhar' para combater crime organizado
item.description: Lula said he asked the Justice Minister to recall Federal Police delegates and agents who are 'pretending to work' to combat organized crime, stressing that all positions should be filled by active servants. He also announced the hiring of 1,000 new federal police officers (630 agents, 160 clerks, 120 delegates, 69 experts, and 21 fingerprint specialists) by year-end. Additionally, he said he will bring jabuticaba to Donald Trump as a gesture to 'calm him down', amid ongoing tensions in Brazil-U.S. bilateral relations.

item.title: É #FAKE que governo Lula abriu comportas do rio São Francisco no Maranhão; vídeo foi gravado no Iêmen
item.description: The video claiming that the Lula government opened the São Francisco River’s floodgates in Maranhão in 2026 for electoral reasons is false. The footage was filmed in Yemen in March 2026, shows gate openings due to seasonal flooding, and contains Arabic audio with no Portuguese narration. The federal government denied the claim, stating no water release occurred for electoral motives.

item.title: Moraes abre prazo para PGR e defesa, e processo contra Eduardo Bolsonaro por coação a autoridades entra na reta final
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes has granted a 15-day window for the Prosecutor General’s Office and Eduardo Bolsonaro’s defense to present final arguments in a case alleging coercion of authorities. Bolsonaro, who resides abroad and has twice waived his right to defend himself, is accused of orchestrating international sanctions — including export tariffs, visa suspensions, and Magnitsky Law applications — to pressure the STF ahead of his father’s trial. The Public Defender’s Office is representing him due to his failure to appoint counsel.

item.title: Gilmar desdenha Zema e diz que mineiro não sabe falar português
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes criticized presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) for his manner of speaking, stating he 'speaks a language close to Portuguese, but which is understood as offensive' in two interviews on the same day. Zema responded on social media, accusing Mendes of elitism and authoritarianism, arguing that the issue is not his speech but the actions of the minister and the STF that alienate power from the people.

item.title: Lula está certo: o campo progressista sucumbiu ao neoliberalismo
item.description: Maria Inês Nassif argues that Brazil's progressive field has succumbed to neoliberalism, validating Lula's critique that the left abandoned principles of social justice and national sovereignty in favor of fiscal adjustments and market alliances. She contends that this subordination weakened structural transformation capacity and left the country vulnerable to conservative setbacks.

item.title: Alerj pede ao STF que Douglas Ruas assuma o governo do Rio
item.description: The Legislative Assembly of Rio de Janeiro (Alerj) filed a request with the Supreme Federal Court (STF) for state deputy Douglas Ruas, elected president of the House, to assume the state government. The argument is that Ruas’s effective inauguration as president of Alerj eliminates the justification for the Rio de Janeiro Court of Justice (TJ-RJ) president, Judge Ricardo Couto, to continue acting as interim governor, a role he assumed due to a vacancy in the state’s constitutional succession line. The request was submitted to Minister Luiz Fux, rapporteur of the case concerning indirect elections in Rio, seeking an immediate and monocratic decision.

item.title: O que é a reciprocidade citada por Lula no caso Ramagem
item.description: President Lula praised the Federal Police's decision to revoke the credentials of a U.S. agent as a measure of reciprocity, in response to the expulsion of a Brazilian delegate operating in Miami linked to the Alexandre Ramage case. Reciprocity, while not a law, is a principle in international relations calling for proportional retaliation to actions by other states. Brazil enacted the Economic Reciprocity Law in April to allow countermeasures against unilateral decisions by other countries that impact national economy and sovereignty.

item.title: TSE mantém direito de preso provisório votar em 2026, mesmo após lei Antifacção
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) ruled to maintain the voting rights of pretrial detainees in the 2026 elections, despite the new Anticorruption Law (Law 15.358/2026) that sought to prohibit voting for anyone imprisoned, regardless of final conviction. The Court determined the law cannot apply to the 2026 election due to the constitutional principle of annuality, which bars electoral law changes from taking effect within one year of an election. The ruling preserves current practices, including setting up polling stations in prisons and conducting voter registration for this population, which numbers around 200,000 individuals in Brazil.
